thread:
incident-bot: Pager: high-severity serving errors in us-west-2 (multiple node flaps)
incident-bot: Symptoms: high OOM rate on serve-prod, CUDA driver warnings, persistent RDMA retransmit spikes. Paging: @oncall_maria
oncall_maria: I'm on it. seeing alerts: 5 nodes reporting container restarts + high GPU mem pressure. starting timeline collection.
alex: Confirmed. k8s events show `OOMKilled` across pod group `serve-group-7` starting ~3640001100. CPU low, mem high.
jia: Noticed a ton of IB retransmit counters on pkey0 -> suspect fabric flapping. Running `ibstat`/`perfquery` now.
netops_kevin: Looking at switch syslogs; some port errors on leaf-12 ports 3/4/5 around that time. Could be microbursts from a rack rebuild.
oncall_maria: Running quick mitigation: marking pods on nodes n-az3-12 and n-az3-14 as unschedulable and draining to move traffic.
marco: Agree drain. Also pushing a temporary route to fallback smaller model variant (serve-small) for traffic from the affected ASG to avoid big KV cache pressure.
ops-eng-aya: Can we drop KVCACHE on the older model instances? That reduces memory footprint.
alex: Yes, we have a runtime flag: `--kv-cache-size=0`. Will push to canary on unaffected nodes first.
jia: Perfquery output (excerpt):
```
Port 3: LinkUp
Port 4: LinkDown
Port 5: LinkErrorCount: 4523
PacketRetransmits: +1280 in last 5m
```
Seems spiky.
netops_kevin: Switch shows intermittent CRC errors, probably NIC <-> cable. Asking on-site to reseat cables on leaf-12 and run `ibdiagnet` sweep.
sre-rotator: Paging rotation: @marco you're taking lead for runtime mitigation; @kevin netops owns fabric diagnostics; @jia keep monitoring counters; @oncall_maria own incident comms and status.
oncall_maria: Status page draft: "We are investigating a network-related degradation impacting model serving in us-west-2; some requests are experiencing errors and increased latency. Engineers are mitigating and routing traffic to fallback variants." Anyone object to posting now?
marco: Post it. Add note that dedicated customers on Dedicated-Prod may see increased tail latency.
oncall_maria: Posted.
jia: Quick local mitigation suggestion: throttle batching and disable prefetch for affected nodes to reduce peak memory usage. Example command in runtime config: `--max-batch-size=8 --prefetch=false`
alex: Pushing a rollout to decrease batch size on the autoscaling group attached to the affected AZ. Doing a canary on 3 nodes.
marco: Canary shows reduced OOMs but still occasional CUDA driver timeouts around `kernel 0x3a`. Logs: `E CUDA: cuCtxSynchronize() timed out`
ops-eng-aya: That often follows heavy packet loss causing retries and duplicated work. If the KV cache retries, it blows memory. Suggest enabling `serve.fallback_to_cpu=true` for pods hitting repeated CUDA errors.
netops_kevin: On-site confirmed loose SFP on leaf-12 port5; tech reseated -> error counters dropping. Running 10m window check.
jia: After reseat, retransmits down from +1280 -> +40 in last 5m.
oncall_maria: Observed immediate drop in new OOMs on two drained nodes, but two other nodes in adjacent rack still flapping.
sre-rotator: We should cordon + replace those adjacent nodes, and schedule a rolling reboot of the affected rack to clear lingering NIC driver states.
marco: Agreed. Also adding a temporary topology rule: `route_policy: prefer-region-us-west-2a, fallback: us-west-2b` to reduce cross-rack chatter for this service.
alex: Reboot started on n-az3-16. Monitoring logs...
incident-bot: Deploybot: rollout 3640001400 to autoscale-group serve-prod-small started by alex
ops-eng-aya: FYI, reduced batch config + kvcache off + fallback_to_cpu applied to canary. Observed request success rate up from 72% -> 94% on canary in 3m.
netops_kevin: Leaf-12 SFP reseat appears to have stabilized port errors. We'll continue cable sweep.
marco: Confirming serving runtime logs show no new `OOMKilled` events on canary. Still seeing a handful of `cuCtx` timeouts from older nodes -> those are getting drained.
oncall_maria: Customer impact summary for post-incident: "For ~18 minutes between 12:03-12:21 UTC customers in us-west-2 experienced increased errors and latency; mitigation included draining affected nodes, switching traffic to a smaller model variant, and reseating a mis-seated SFP on leaf-12. No customer data was exposed. We will follow up with RCA." Any changes?
ops-eng-aya: Add note that Dedicated customers may have seen degraded throughput but we engaged on their support channels.
marco: Also add that KV cache config change was temporary and will be reverted after fabric sweep.
jia: Netops: continuing sweep on adjacent racks. If we still see CRCs after 30m, plan is to escalate to vendor and schedule hot-swap.
sre-rotator: Handing off to night oncall: @oncall_maria will create a followup ticket with actions: vendor escalation if CRC persists, node reboots for any nodes with repeated `cuCtx` timeouts, validate autoscaling policies to prevent over-packing of large models during network instability.
oncall_maria: Created ticket INF-4821 with links to perfquery logs and runtime dumps. Assigning to netops_kevin and marco.
netops_kevin: Acknowledged. Continuing monitoring.
marco: Putting a brief postmortem stub: cause = intermittent fabric errors (loose SFP) causing packet retransmits -> duplicated retries and KV cache growth -> GPU memory pressure -> container OOMs and CUDA timeouts -> node flaps.
oncall_maria: Thanks all. Leaving incident channel open for any residual observations.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: severity lowered to P2 at 3640003200. Follow-up: RCA and vendor escalation if any new CRCs within 72h.
